items.question: Proposed question: Does the build use machine-state lifecycle operations - pause, resume, and fork of a paused sandbox - where the isolation class offers them, and is it free of the errors the window has ruled out?
items.target: Suspension, resumption and forking are capability operations with a defined answer when an adapter cannot serve them, and the security boundary chosen for untrusted output is not a shared kernel.

items.question: Proposed: Is the production of the failure object owned by one place the core imports, so a new capability adapter cannot invent its own failure shape?
items.target: Adapters raise typed conditions that the shared construction point renders; there is no second place a failure body is built.

items.question: Can it be shown that no artifact escapes the guarantee, that every artifact produced over a period has a record, and that a component cannot produce one through a path which emits nothing? (This question is proposed, derived from the row it cites.)
items.target: The two counts reconcile with no unattested artifact; emission is wired where every producing path passes, so a component that attests nothing itself still yields a record; the attempt to write outside that path is refused or is structurally impossible.
